references.text: Shows that Noah followed God's command in Gen 6:19 by taking pairs of clean and unclean animals, birds, and creeping things into the ark.
Confirms the fulfillment of the command in Gen 6:19: pairs of all flesh, male and female, entered the ark as God had commanded.
Direct continuation of v.19 specifying which types of animals—birds, livestock, and creeping things—were to come to Noah in pairs into the ark.
Expands on the command from 6:19 with details about the number of clean animals (seven pairs) and unclean animals (one pair) to be taken into the ark.
Noah's faith and obedience to God's command, including instructions to preserve life in the ark, are highlighted as an example of faith.
This reference shows how the general plan of salvation in chapter 6 is made concrete with ritual requirements in chapter 7.
The verse extends the general command about 'all living things' to include birds with specific numerical rules for preservation.
This verse completes the theological cycle by showing that the animals saved into the ark are now released to fill the earth again.
